lines.li: [them] If our families ever make a match of this, I'd want it done properly.
[us] Then I'll speak for it properly, when you're ready.
[them,their:lowtech] Not yet, the old ones need to get used to your face first.
[them] Not yet, let me tell my people first.
[them] My family keeps asking why I find so many reasons to visit your colony.
[us] What do you tell them?
[them] That your cook is very good.
[us] How old are your people when they marry?
[them,their:tribal] Old enough that the elders say so, and they are in no hurry.
[them,their:medieval] Young, if the house has land, and later if it hasn't.
[them,their:hightech] Whenever the paperwork's done, which is never quick.
[them] Whenever they find the right one, or give up looking.
[them] A titled colonist could make a fine match at court, you know.
[us] I'm not looking.
[them] At court, the best matches are made by people who weren't looking.
[them] Our people haven't married outside our own in a long time.
[us] Then we'll try to do it justice.
[them,their:lowtech] Do that, and the old ones will talk of it for years.
[them] Do that, and they'll be telling the story for years.
[them] Not everyone at home is pleased about this match.
[us] Not everyone here is, either.
[them] Then it should suit both sides.
[them] Our side read the terms twice and found nothing to argue about.
[us] Is that rare?
[them] Very, and it's making the lawyers nervous.
[them] The household is choosing what to wear, which may take longer than the match did.
[us] Tell them there's no need to dress up for us.
[them] There is always a need, and they would never forgive me.
[them] The old ones are arguing over which songs belong at a wedding with outsiders.
[us] Is there a right answer?
[them] There will be, once one of them wins.
[them] At home they're counting out the dowry again, in case they got it wrong.
[us] Did they?
[them] No, but the counting is half the pleasure.
[them] The whole family has an opinion about the wedding, and most of them are kind.
[us] And the rest?
[them] The rest are my uncle's, and he has opinions about everything.
[us] Has {SPOUSEOF} found their feet among you yet?
[them,their:tribal] {SPOUSEOF} sleeps at our fire now, and the dogs have stopped barking at them.
[them,their:medieval] {SPOUSEOF} got lost in our market twice, and asked the way like a local the third time.
[them] Nearly, there's a lot of family to learn the names of.
[us] Give them time.
[them] How has {INLAW} taken to your colony, now the wedding's behind them?
[us] Better than we hoped, and we hoped a lot.
[them] Good, the house is quiet without {INLAW}.
[them] I've brought news from home for {INLAW}, if you know where they are.
[us] Around somewhere, ask anyone, they'll point you.
[them] Then I'll go looking, it's mostly gossip anyway.
[them] Home sends its love, and a list of things you forgot to take.
[us] Tell them I'm well, and that I eat better here than I did at home.
[them] I'll tell them the first half.
[us] Does {SPOUSEOF} ever talk about coming back to visit?
[them,their:tribal] At every full moon, and then the hunting starts and the moon is forgotten.
[them] Often, but there's always work, and the road is long.
[us] Tell them the gate here is always open.
[them] {SPOUSEOF} works with the rest of us now, and doesn't complain about the hours.
[us] Then they've changed since they left us.
[them] Marriage will do that.
[them] Is {INLAW} pulling their weight here?
[us] More than, and complaining less than most.
[them] Then your colony has done what we never could.
[us] What do your people expect of in-laws?
[them,their:tribal] A place at the fire when we visit, and help with the hunt when we ask.
[them,their:medieval] A seat at the table, a gift at midwinter, and no arguing with the old ones.
[them,their:industrial] A letter now and then, and help when the caravan breaks down.
[them,their:empire] Correct forms of address, and attendance when it is asked for.
[them,their:spacer,!their:empire] Courtesy, and that you keep your records straight.
[them] To be remembered, mostly.
[us] We can manage that.
[them] Are you happy, married into all this?
[us,us:spousehere] Ask me again when {OURSPOUSE} stops stealing the blankets.
[us] I am, most days, and the other days are my own fault.
[them] Spoken like someone properly married.
[them] Not everyone at home was glad of your match.
[us] They weren't asked.
[them] That's what they're unhappy about.
[them] My people will come when you call, the marriage says so.
[us] I hope we never need to.
[them,their:lowtech] Kin don't wait to be asked twice.
[them] So do I, but they'll come all the same.
[them] The Empire signs no pacts, but a household never forgets its in-laws.
[us] We'll try to be worth remembering.
[them] Our people have been watching that {RAIDCAMP} for you, as kin should.
[us] Then tell us if it moves.
[them] You'll hear before anyone.
[them] We heard about the raid, and the first thing anyone at home asked was after {INLAW}.
[us] I'll tell {INLAW} you were worried.
[them] Do, it'll mean more coming from you.
[them] We heard about {DEAD}, and our people grieve with yours.
[us] Thank you, it helps to hear it from family.
[them] You have some nerve, talking to me.
[us] Somebody from this colony has to.
[them] I hold this grudge for my people, and I'll hand it on if I have to.
[us] Is there nothing that would end it?
[them] Nothing your colony has offered.
[us] How do your people settle a wrong like this?
[them,their:tribal] Blood for blood, the old ones say, though the young aren't so sure.
[them,their:medieval] In the old days with a blood price, but our head hasn't named one, and won't.
[them,their:industrial] In a court, if there were one, and there isn't.
[them,their:spacer,!their:empire] There is no procedure for it, which is the problem.
[them] We don't settle it, we carry it.
[us] Then I hope we find a way, one day.
[them] We were family once, through that marriage.
[us] We could be again, if both sides wanted it.
[them] Maybe, but not this year.
